question.text: In an ordinary annuity, payments are made:

answer.text: At the beginning of each period
At the end of each period
In the middle of each period
In a lump sum at the end of the total period

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 41 of the workbook states that ordinary annuity payments are made at the end of the relevant period. Bond coupons are a common example. The Trap: Annuity due — covered on page 42 — has payments at the start of the period, not the end. The timing difference materially affects valuation. Note: Get the timing right (end-of-period vs start-of-period) before applying any PV/FV annuity formula, as the same cashflows discount to different values under the two conventions.
